PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The proposed project is a request for the continued operation of two monopoles for an
existing major wireless telecommunications facility located at 41343 12th Street West for
a period of 10 years. The facility was previously approved as a 65-foot-high monopole
with a 234 square foot equipment enclosure with a 684 square foot lease area.

BACKGROUND

On February 20, 2003, the Planning Commission approved CUP 02-11 (Resolution No.
PC-2003-018), which allowed for the construction of a major wireless telecommunication
facility consisting of a 65-foot-high monopole and a 234 square foot equipment enclosure
with a 684 square foot lease area. On September 7, 2006, the Planning Commission
approved CUP 02-11 Major Modification (Resolution No. PC-2006-087) for the
construction of a second 65-foot-high monopole disguised as a flagpole.

Pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section 17.95.040.A, major wireless
telecommunications facilities expire after a period of 10 years, unless a time extension is
approved. Since a time extension application was not received prior to expiration of the
major wireless telecommunications facility, the entitlement expired, and a new CUP is
required for the continued operation of the facility.

The existing facility has been modified four times since the original approval, through
Minor Modifications (MM):

    MM13-054 approved on October 15, 2013;
    MM14-014 approved on May 13, 2014;
    MM20-047 approved on November 4, 2020; and,
    MM22-049 approved on February 16, 2023.

The subject application was initially submitted on March 1, 2023, and was deemed
incomplete. After resolution of completeness items, the application was deemed
complete October 5, 2023, and scheduled for the October 12, 2023, Planning
Commission meeting.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

An Initial Study was prepared for the project in conjunction with the original approval and
on February 20, 2003, the Planning Commission adopted an MND finding that, with the
incorporation of mitigation measures, the project would not have a significant impact on
the environment. Staff has reviewed the MND to determine whether the project triggered
any of the conditions described in Sections 15162, 15163, and 15164 of the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines and determined that additional
documentation is not required for the project because CUP 23-006 does not propose any
significant revisions to the project, there are no changes in circumstances and there is no
new information of substantial importance that will involve new significant environmental
effects or increase the severity of previously identified significant effects. The proposed
project is a request for the continued operation of two monopoles at an existing major
wireless telecommunications facility and does not include any alterations to the facility as
approved through CUP 02-11 and CUP 02-11MM. Furthermore, a Radio Frequency
report was submitted as part of the mitigation monitoring program and shows that the
project will continue to be compliant with Federal Communications Commission rules and
regulations, as described in Office of Engineering and Technology Bulletin 65.

OPTIONS

The Planning Commission has the following options:

1.  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2023-023 approving CUP 23-006 and find that the
  project is consistent with the previously adopted MND and MMRP.

2.  Continue the project and direct staff to return with additional information.

3.  Deny the project.

Option 1 is recommended.

Some members of the public have generated debate regarding the issue
of health effects caused by electromagnetic energy used in wireless
communications systems. The public's concern revolves around whether
the type of energy emitted by these systems affect humans and causes
illnesses.

There are three wireless communications sources that generate and use
electromagnetic energy: Call site antennas, hand-held portable
communications devices, and electrical equipment in equipment buildings
at call sites and switching stations.

Electromagnetic energy exists in a variety of forms, including radio and
television waves, microwaves, heat lamp radiation, visible and ultraviolet
light, and electrical currents passing through wires.  Whenever
electromagnetic energy moves from one point to another through
electrical wires, the movement is accompanied by the formation of electric
and magnetic fields (also referred to as electromagnetic fields, or EMF5).
Whenever electromagnetic energy moves from one point to another by
waves propagated through space, the movement is accompanied by the
formation or radiofrequency radiation (RFR).

EMF5 have been the subject of recent scientific and public interest
because of some epidemiological studies suggesting a link between EMF
exposures and certain types of health concerns. Health concerns about
EMF5 have centered around high-power electrical sources, such as high-
voltage electrical transmission lines. However, the EMFs associated with
electrical equipment used in wireless communications systems such as
pumps, motors, switches, and telephones are relatively low intensity and
generally not considered a health problem.

All forms of transmitted electromagnetic energy travel at the speed of
light.  Depending on how it was generated and transmitted,
radiofrequency radiation (RFR) will radiate outward from the source in

Radiation can be broadly broken into two groupings: ionizing and non-
ionizing. Ionizing means that there is enough energy in the radiation to
alter the chemical structure of matter upon its absorption to knock off
electrically charged particles (ions). Non-ionizing means that there is not
enough energy in the radiation to create ions. Instead, the energy is
usually absorbed as heat. RFR is a form of non-ionizing radiation.

Electromagnetic waves of lower frequency levels and energies, such as
RFR and EMFs associated with radio systems, do not cause ionization
and consequently are referred to as "non-ionizing" radiation (NIER). If
absorbed at all, this type of energy is absorbed as heat.  Unless
generated at extremely high power densities and at just the right
resonance frequencies so as to produce large amounts of heat resulting in
actual burns, the frequency and resulting energy levels of non-ionizing
radiation are almost always too low to affect biological materials.

Non-ionizing radiation is not known to damage DNA as can ionizing
radiation, and generally has not been shown to cause irreversible changes
that can accumulate over time. However, sometimes in a complex

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The proposed project is a request for the continued operation of an existing major wireless
telecommunications facility for a period of 10 years located at 2200 East Avenue S. The
facility was previously approved as three 60-foot-high slimline monopoles and a 230
square foot equipment enclosure. The existing facility consists of three slimline
monopoles painted green, each housing four panel antennas for a total of 12 antennas,
six cabinets, one generator, one concrete masonry unit (CMU) equipment enclosure, and
a six foot high wrought iron fence with concrete masonry block pilasters surrounding an
approximately 1,345 square foot lease area at the subject site. The applicant is not
proposing to expand the lease area. The current carrier at the existing facility is AT&T.

BACKGROUND

On June 1, 2006, the Planning Commission approved CUP 05-021 (Resolution No.
PC-2006-045), which allowed for the construction of a major wireless telecommunications
facility consisting of three 60-foot-high monopoles and a 230 square foot equipment
enclosure with an expiration date of June 13, 2016. On July 12, 2018, the Planning
Commission approved CUP 18-003 and Site Plan Review (SPR) 18-019, which was a
request to replace the existing major wireless telecommunications facility with one
monopole disguised as a faux pine tree with an inauguration deadline of July 24, 2021.
The approvals were not inaugurated by the deadline and subsequently expired. On
July 22, 2021, Crown Castle submitted an SPR application (SPR 21-007) to the Planning
Division along with the CUP 21-007 to continue the use of the existing facility, modify the
existing facility to disguise the slimline monopoles as faux cypress trees and establish a
new carrier. After resolution of completeness items, the application was deemed complete
on August 31, 2023, and scheduled for the October 12, 2023, Planning Commission
hearing.

Pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section 17.95.040.A, wireless
telecommunications facilities expire after a period of 10 years, unless a time extension is
approved. Since a time extension application was not received by the Planning Division
prior to expiration of the facility, the entitlement expired, and a new CUP is required for
the continued operation of the facility. The applicant has not proposed to expand the lease
area of the existing major wireless telecommunications facility.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), an Initial Study was
prepared for the project in conjunction with the original approval and on June 1, 2006, the
Planning Commission adopted a Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) finding that, with
the incorporation of mitigation measures, the project would not have a significant impact
on the environment. Staff has reviewed the MND and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting
Program (MMRP) to determine whether the project triggered any of the conditions
described in Sections 15162, 15163, and 15164 of the CEQA Guidelines and determined
that additional documentation is not required for the project because CUP 21-007 does
not propose any significant revisions to the project, there are no changes in
circumstances and there is no new information of substantial importance that will involve
new significant environmental effects or increase the severity of previously identified
significant effects. As previously mentioned, the applicant has not proposed to expand
the existing facility. The proposed project is a request to continue the operation of an
existing major wireless telecommunications facility and does not include any alterations
to the major wireless telecommunications facility as approved through CUP 05-021.
Furthermore, a Radio Frequency report was submitted as part of the mitigation monitoring
program and shows that the project will continue to be compliant with Federal
Communications Commission rules and regulations, as described in the Office of
Engineering and Technology Bulletin 65.
